'''Robert Whyte''' (born 1955, in Melbourne) is an Australian writer. He was a founding co-owner and director of the Brisbane-based multimedia firm ToadShow. After 2012 he participated in the Australian Government's new species exploration program [[Bush Blitz]]. His works include ''The Creek in Our Back Yard: a practical guide to creek restoration'' (2011)<ref name=":0">"The creek in our back yard" {{ISBN|978-0-646-55158-6}}. Save Our Waterways Now Inc | ABN 78 309 030 727 http://saveourwaterwaysnow.com.au/01_cms/details.asp?ID=2340 and second edition revised and expanded June 2013 {{ISBN|978-0-646-90214-2}} http://saveourwaterwaysnow.com.au/01_cms/details.asp?ID=2423</ref> and ''A Field Guide to Spiders of [[Australia]]''<ref name=":1" /> for [[CSIRO Publishing|CSIRO Publishing 2017]].

==Biography==
[[File:robertwhyte photo mark crocker reupload.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Robert Whyte delivering a paper on invertebrate biodiversity Photo: Mark Crocker<ref>"Take a closer look: observations of a digital naturalist" http://www.saveourwaterwaysnow.com.au/_dbase_upl/spidiversity_005-lo.pdf</ref> at the Brisbane City Council's 2010 Biodiversity Forum]]Robert Whyte was born in Melbourne in 1955.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=http://remix.org.au/artist-profile-robert-whyte/|title=Robert WHYTE|date=2015-11-04|work=ARI Remix: Living Archives, Artist-Runs 1980-2000 Qld, NSW, ACT|access-date=2017-05-13|language=en-US}}</ref> His family moved to Brisbane in 1957.

In 1976 he was awarded a One Year Young Writer's Fellowship by the Literature Board of the [[Australia Council for the Arts]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.austlit.edu.au/austlit/page/A28986|title=Robert John Whyte: (author/organisation) {{!}} AustLit: Discover Australian Stories|last=Austlit|website=www.austlit.edu.au|language=en|access-date=2017-12-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://remix.org.au/artist-profile-robert-whyte/|title=Robert WHYTE|date=2015-11-04|work=ARI Remix: Living Archives, Artist-Runs 1980-2000 Qld, NSW, ACT|access-date=2017-12-11|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 1981 he completed a Postgraduate Diploma in Professional Art Studies at Alexander Mackie CAE (now University of Western Sydney), and was a contributor to Sydney art magazine ''Art Network''.

In 1985 he undertook the production of ''Environment Victoria'', the magazine of the Conservation Council of Victoria, now [[Environment Victoria]]. In 1987 he was founding co-editor of contemporary art magazine ''Eyeline'' with Sarah Follent and Graham Coulter-Smith.<ref>Queensland Artworkers Alliance.  1987  Eyeline [http://nla.gov.au/nla.cat-vn101743 National Library]</ref>

Robert Whyte was a co-owner of ToadShow,  a multimedia firm in Brisbane, Queensland.<ref>Jordan, Peter 2007 Career FAQs Digital Media {{ISBN|1-921106-49-2}}</ref> 
As a web designer he was responsible for ''Brisbane Stories'' a collection of web sites revealing stories of hidden Brisbane featuring art, environment and history.<ref>Brisbane Stories http://www.brisbane-stories.webcentral.com.au/</ref>

Robert Whyte was an editor of ''[[The Cane Toad Times]]'' from 1985 to 1990.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.slq.qld.gov.au/cane-toad-times/ctt|title=Cane Toad Times|last=jurisdiction=Queensland|first=corporateName=State Library of Queensland|website=www.slq.qld.gov.au|language=en|access-date=2017-04-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.toadshow.com.au/cane-toad-times/|title=Cane Toad Times Warts and All Best of Collection 1977-1990|website=www.toadshow.com.au|access-date=2017-04-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Poking Fun in a Police State|last=Whyte|first=Robert|publisher=State Library of Queensland|year=2011|isbn=9780975803080|location=Brisbane}}</ref> Between 2002 and 2019 he undertook habitat restorations projects in [[South East Queensland]].<ref>[http://www.creekrescue.com.au Creek Rescue and Catchment Care (CRACC)]</ref> In 2011 his book ''The creek in our backyard: A practical guide for landholders''<ref>{{Cite book|title=The creek in our backyard : a practical guide for landholders|last=Robert.|first=Whyte|date=2011|publisher=Save Our Waterways Now Inc|others=Save Our Waterways Now (Organisation)|isbn=9780646551586|location=The Gap, Qld.|oclc=780532080}}</ref> was published, an expanded second edition appearing in 2013<ref>{{Cite book|title=The creek in our backyard : a practical guide for habitat restoration|last=Robert|first=Whyte|others=Save Our Waterways Now (Organisation)|date=10 April 2024 |isbn=9780646902142|edition=Second edition revised and expanded June 2013|location=The Gap, Queensland|oclc=856951935}}</ref> ''A field guide to the spiders of Australia'' for CSIRO Publishing was released 1 June 2017.<ref name=":1">"A field Guide to the Spiders of Australia" for CSIRO Publishing http://www.arachne.org.au</ref><ref name="Whyte">{{Cite book|url=http://www.publish.csiro.au/book/6899/|title=A Field Guide to Spiders of Australia|last1=Whyte|first1=Robert|last2=Anderson|first2=Greg|date=2017-06-01}}</ref>

== Bush Blitz ==
[[File:Bush Blitz team at Kiwirrkurra Indigenous Protected area in the Gibson Desert WA. .jpg|alt=Robert Whyte at Kiwirrkurra|thumb|Robert Whyte far right with the Bush Blitz team in Kiwirrkurra Indigenous Protected Area Gibson Desert  WA. |200x200px]]
Robert Whyte participated in the Australian Government's new species exploration program [[Bush Blitz]] from 2012's [[Fish River Station|Fish River Bush Blitz]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://bushblitz.gaiaresources.com.au/fish-river-station-nt-2012/|title=Fish River Station NT, 2012 - BushBlitz|date=2013-09-15|work=BushBlitz|access-date=2017-04-14|language=en-US}}</ref> as a scientist specialising in [[spider]]s and as a scientific photographer. In 2013 he attended the [[Henbury Station]] Bush Blitz<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://bushblitz.gaiaresources.com.au/henbury-station-nt-2013/|title=Henbury Station NT, 2013 - BushBlitz|date=2014-12-18|work=BushBlitz|access-date=2017-04-15|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/robertwhyte/albums/72157633501389807|title=Henbury Station Bush Blitz 2013 Jo Harding|website=Flickr|date=17 May 2013 |language=en-us|access-date=2017-04-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/robertwhyte/albums/72157633499419068|title=Henbury Station Bush Blitz 2013|website=Flickr|date=12 May 2013 |language=en-us|access-date=2017-04-15}}</ref> in the [[Northern Territory]]. In 2014 he participated as scientist and photographer at the Home Valley Bush Blitz<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://au.earthwatch.org/News-Media/greatest-species-discovery-in-western-australia-in-10-years|title=Greatest Species Discovery in Western Australia in 10 Years|work=earthwatch|access-date=2017-04-15|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.environment.gov.au/minister/birmingham/2014/mr20140603.html|title=New species discovered on Kimberley Bush Blitz - Media release 3 June 2014|website=www.environment.gov.au|language=en|access-date=2017-04-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://shaesbushblitz.weebly.com|title=Bush Blitz TeachLive 2014|website=Bush Blitz TeachLive 2014|access-date=2017-04-15}}</ref> in The Kimberly, Western Australia and in 2015 participated in the [[Kiwirrkurra Community, Western Australia|Kiwirrkurra]] IPA Bush Blitz in the [[Gibson Desert]] in [[Western Australia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.toadshow.com.au/portfolio/project.asp?ID=79#|title=Kiwirrkurra Bush Blitz - ToadShow - Graphic design, web design, multimedia, creative communications, Toowong, Queensland|website=www.toadshow.com.au|access-date=2017-04-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/centraldesertlandandcommunity/posts/948861515159569|title=Central Desert Land and Community Team|website=www.facebook.com|language=en|access-date=2017-04-15}}</ref> In 2017 he attended the Bush Blitz, in Quinkan Country inland from [[Cooktown, Queensland|Cooktown]] on [[Cape York Peninsula]], where he photographed and filmed live spiders  discovered on the trip.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2017-04-13|title=Spider photographer documents discovery of 56 new species|language=en-AU|work=ABC News|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-04-13/spider-species-discovery-far-north-queensland/8443024|access-date=2017-04-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Media centre - BushBlitz|language=en-US|work=BushBlitz|url=http://bushblitz.org.au/media-centre/|access-date=2017-04-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Ten|first=Network|title=New Spider Species|url=https://tenplay.com.au/channel-ten/the-project/extra/season-8/new-spider-species|access-date=2017-04-14|website=TenPlay - New Spider Species}}</ref>

In September 2018 Robert Whyte’s discovered 37 new spider species leading the spider team as part of the fauna, flora and fungi stocktake led by John Sinclair of the Fraser Island Defenders Organisation<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fido.org.au|title=Fraser Island Defenders Organisation – FIDO, "The Watchdog of Fraser Island", aims to ensure the wisest use of Fraser Island's natural resources.|website=fido.org.au|language=en-US|access-date=2018-11-02}}</ref> in conjunction with Cooloola Coast Care.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cooloolacoastcare.org.au|title=Cooloola Coastcare|website=www.cooloolacoastcare.org.au|language=en-US|access-date=2018-11-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-09-28/new-spider-species-found-cooloola-coast/10312042|title=Thirty-seven new spider species discovered in Queensland|date=2018-09-28|work=ABC News|access-date=2018-11-02|language=en-AU}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Robert Whyte|title=37 new spider species from Cooloola 2018 BioBlitz|date=2018-09-28|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=41_LD_XQOOc |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/41_LD_XQOOc |archive-date=2021-12-15 |url-status=live|access-date=2018-11-02}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://au.news.yahoo.com/meet-creepy-crawly-prince-darkness-dozens-new-aussie-spiders-found-000045183.html|title=Meet the creepy crawly prince of darkness: Dozens of new Aussie spiders found|access-date=2018-11-02|language=en-AU}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=Dozens of new spiders species discovered in Sunshine state 28/09/2018|date=2018-09-28|url=http://www.abc.net.au/newsradio/content/s4901508.htm|language=en-AU|access-date=2018-11-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/cooloolacoastcare.org.au/coastcare-redesign/projects/bioblitz/media|title=Cooloola Coastcare - Media|website=sites.google.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-11}}</ref>

== ''A Field Guide to Spiders of Australia'' ==
Whyte and Anderson's ''A Field Guide to Spiders of Australia'' was published in 2017 by CSIRO Publishing (with foreword by [[Tim Low]]). The [[News.com.au|News Network news.com.au]] report on "Five reasons why you shouldn't be afraid of spiders" was based on the content of the book.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.news.com.au/technology/science/animals/queensland-museum-spider-experts-explains-why-we-shouldnt-be-scared-of-spiders/news-story/c5498d483a90d05213579e6973835b6b|title=How you can cure your spider phobia|work=NewsComAu|access-date=2017-06-22|language=en}}</ref> On 4 May 2018 Robert Whyte appeared on [[Gardening Australia]] as a “My Garden Path” presenter, explaining the link between spider diversity and healthy gardens.<ref>{{Citation|title=My Garden Path - Robert Whyte|date=2018-05-10|url=http://www.abc.net.au/gardening/factsheets/my-garden-path-robert-whyte/9728848|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|language=en|access-date=2018-05-09}}</ref>

== Publishing ==
In 2019 Whyte started a new venture called h.a.r.p.o. (How About Resisting Powerful Organisations) to publish books featuring [[Brisbane]], especially Brisbane [[Noir fiction|Noir]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Steger|first=Jason|date=February 22–23, 2020|title=Harpo's marks|work=The Sydney Morning Herald, Spectrum}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=h.a.r.p.o. Publishing|url=https://www.h-a-r-p-o.com.au}}</ref>
